rv.q: As far as drama on which to hang ideas (and showcase such stage virtuosity), “This Much I Know” is a eureka moment.
Ultimately, you emerge from the theatre buzzy from ideas, dizzy from the plot, fizzy from the entertainment.
But we’re ultimately less invested in the stories themselves than the ideas they demonstrate.

That’s a shame, because the production, under Hayley Finn’s excellent direction—she also helmed the show at Theater J in Washington, D.C.—manages to bring Spector’s formidable script to often compelling life, thanks in large part to three committed, and elastic, performers.

cn.t: Spector's ambitious, erudite play about cognition and behavior challenges audiences with its intellectual scope. Critics find it tantalizing if occasionally baffling, praising its Stoppardian range but noting it demands patience.
